sanjay: Heads up — noticed a regression in TP + fused flash-attn when KV cache is enabled. All-gather latency on QKV spikes and end-to-end token latency +20%.

sanjay: Profiling snippet:
```
qkv_allgather: 0.8ms -> 3.6ms per step
end_to_end: 34.1ms -> 42.0ms (+23%)
seq_len=2048, tp=2, batch=8
```
eva: Oof. Is this tied to batch shapes or seq length? What config did you run?
sanjay: tp=2, pp=1, local_batch=4 (global 8), seq=2048, head_dim=64, fp16, kv_cache=on, model=redwood-3b-fused
lee: My hunch: kernel selector falls back to non-flash path when local seq/head alignment is off. Seen odd behavior when seqs land on shard boundaries (remainder handling). Can you try seq=2047 or pad to 2050 to see diff?
morgan: Ran a quick nsys capture — NVLINK utilization drops during the qkv exchange window. Summary:
```
nsys summary:
qkv_exchange window: 2.9-3.7ms
GPU0 idle during exchange: 42%
allreduce stalls: visible on gaps between compute kernels
```
perf-bot: [alert] regression-detector: +22% latency on redwood-3b-fused (2026-03-15T10:12Z)
sanjay: I think the kernel picker marks flash-attn incompatible when local_kv_stride != expected and falls back to elementwise qkv kernels. Patch idea: prefer flash path when (local_head_dim % warp_width == 0) OR pad local seq to warp multiple using transient buffer. Pseudopatch:
```
if (can_pad_to_warp(seq)) use_flash_with_padding(); else fallback();
```
eva: Padding works but costs extra token compute. Could we instead change the allgather schedule to aggregate by head-chunk to reduce per-allgather payloads? Might reduce peak NVLINK pressure.
lee: Aggregating by head reduces message size but increases number of launches and scatter ops. That could increase kernel-launch overhead on small batches. We should microbenchmark head-split vs shard-split.
morgan: I'll run microbench tomorrow across tp={1,2,4}, batch={4,8,16}, seq={1024,1536,2048} and post nsys + nvvp captures. Meanwhile, adding a temporary routing rule: if qkv_allgather > 2ms then route to single-shard flash variant to avoid tail latencies.
lee: Also saw KV-cache prefetch thrashing when requests have variable prefix lengths — prefetcher issues many small fetches that contend on NVLink. Grouping by prefix length helps but can increase queueing latency.
sanjay: Noted. Another mitigation: router-level grouping of similar prefix-length requests so prefetcher can amortize. Router change looks like: group_key = floor(prefix_len/64).
eva: Grouping helps hit-rate but adds head-of-line for mixed workloads. Alternative: background prefetch with rate limiter per-GPU.
lee: Filing bug for flash-attn edge-case: when head_dim % 32 != 0 we get non-coalesced loads and fallback kernels. Repro command I used:
```
python -m perf_test --model redwood-3b-fused --tp 2 --head-dim 70 --seq 2048 --kv-cache on
```
sanjay: Created issue #2147 for kernel-selector + padding + head-dim pathology. Uploaded nsys capture to S3: https://s3.redwood.internal/perf/1958001122/nsys-capture-2147 (public link internal-only).
deploy-bot: deploy queued: perf-experiments/pad-flash-kv @ 1958001300 — running canary to validate padding approach
morgan: I'll run the bench suite against the canary and post numbers here once complete :eyes:
